title: EaW/FoC LSP schema - tag file
description: Shape of eaw/tags/*.yaml and foc/tags/*.yaml. Mirrors YamlTagFile/YamlTagEntry in PG.StarWarsGame.LSP.Schema. The C# parser is deliberately lenient - an unknown 'type' skips the tag entirely, an unknown referenceKind/semanticType/variantMode falls back to a default, and unmatched keys are ignored (IgnoreUnmatchedProperties) - all with nothing louder than a log warning. This schema is therefore stricter than the parser on purpose: it fails the build on exactly the mistakes that would otherwise ship silently.

localisedText.description: Locale code -> text. 'en' is the fallback the server resolves against.

tag.description: The XML element name, verbatim including casing.

type.description: XmlValueType member. An unknown value makes the parser skip the tag entirely, so the tag would simply not exist.

referenceType.description: The reference target. With referenceKind xmlObject it names the object type (e.g. GameObjectType, Faction, SFXEvent); with workspaceFile it names the file type in the file-type registry (e.g. StoryPlotManifest, StoryParser, LuaScript).

enumName.description: Enum this tag's value belongs to. Must name a file in enums/.

valueGroup.description: Validation group membership - a single group or a list of them.

multipleAllowed.description: True when the element may legitimately appear more than once on one object. Also selects append-vs-union semantics for variantMode: merge.

allOf.$comment: An enum reference with no enumName resolves against nothing at all. The converse is deliberately NOT enforced: tuple-valued tags (HardPointSfxMap, AbilityModMultiplier, ...) carry enumName to document the enum of one slot, without the whole value being an enum reference.

then.$comment: enumName is redeclared here only to satisfy ajv's strictRequired check.

referenceKind.description: ReferenceKind member. Two notes on what is accepted here. First, 'unknown' is not an enum member - the parser falls back to None - but it is used ~80 times across the repo as a deliberate 'not yet classified' marker. Second, the parser matches case-insensitively and the repo genuinely mixes casing (xmlObject/XmlObject, HardcodedSet/hardcodedSet), so both forms are listed rather than forcing a repo-wide reformat. The point is to reject names that are simply wrong, not to enforce a house style.

variantMode.description: How a Variant_Of_Existing_Type variant applies this tag over its base.

semanticType.description: Both casings are listed because the parser matches case-insensitively and the repo genuinely mixes them (FlagList and ownerScopedReference both occur).
